title: What are your thoughts on My Fair Lady?

commenti.body: It’s one of my favourites!  It also holds a special place in my heart as the first movie I was allowed to watch that had cursing in it.  The script is hilarious; the songs are tuneful and fun. Rex Harrison’s performance and Cecil Beaton’s costumes are exquisite.  Audrey Hepburn and her voice dubber Marni Nixon are great too.

I haven’t seen it in over 30 years. It’s a lovely film. But in hindsight it does have a couple of issues. If Rex Harrison couldn’t sing, why not dub him too? Sing speaking was quite a choice! As far as the ending, am I remembering this correctly? Having become a perfectly trained subservient, he asks her to fetch his slippers? And we’re supposed to think that’s romantic? A life of being ordered around. Quite an antiquated message. It would have been much better if Eliza lovingly smiled, then with a beautiful English accent went, “Eat shit, darling.”

Even as a kid, that ending is wonky. This dude got this fine piece of… person. And he’s still going to treat her like crap? He’s been having anger management issues throughout the entire film, but he’ll settle down his nerves now that Eliza is his slave?

Well the film has many unforgettable scenes, like the race scene. And Marnie Nixon did a great job! If you enjoyed her voice, I’d suggest her Fauré album. If Firestone at NEC still keeps records, it quite lovely on vinyl.

I really love My Fair Lady and Audrey, but the whole romance thing doesn’t really work and same with ending apparently it’s different in the book (i haven’t read it). Age gap is too big and there’s no chemistry whatsoever, it’s really more of a case of old professor Higgins getting fired up by this new project, I wish they could have done a different ending. But Eliza’s transformation and ball scene and races are very funny and  costumes are so so gorgeous. It’s one of those films I’m happy to watch over and over again without paying too much attention to flaws.

> As far as the ending, am I remembering this correctly? Having become a perfectly trained subservient, he asks her to fetch his slippers? And we’re supposed to think that’s romantic?

I don’t think you’re being entirely fair to the movie here. He *does* ask her to fetch his slippers, but it’s kind of a comical pretend blasé response. He was missing her, literally listening to records of her talking when she walks in. Then he’s like “Oh, there you are. Wasn’t concerned at all really. Now go on and get my slippers.” And Eliza realizes that, which is why she just smiles at him.

You, of course, still don’t have to like this ending, but I don’t think it’s this heavily misogynist message.

I also enjoy Rex Harrison’s patter singing, which I think really fits the way his numbers are written, as well as his character. I can see how this wouldn’t be to everyone’s taste. However, considering he was in the stage show (and cast recordings thereof), I would find it incredibly odd if they had dubbed him, as would audiences of the time.

It has some story issues and kinda falls apart near the end, but it's a fun watch for sure. I personally think the whole thing is worth it for the "Ascot Gavotte" scene; the way the mannered, straight-faced appearance and movement of the people juxtaposes with their descriptions of thrill and excitement is absolutely hilarious, and perfectly emphasizes the themes of the film.

I do like my fair lady but I think it winning best picture over Mary Poppins is one of the biggest snubs in oscar history. I mean it wasn't even the best musical of that year lol. I wouldn't have minded Dr Strangelove either but between MFL and MP it's a p clear winner.

Yes, the original play had a much better ending, but the movie went with a completely ridiculous crowd-pleasing ending which undercuts the movie quite a bit. If you just stop the movie 2-3 minutes before the credits it's much better.

We need alternative cut! It’s also confusing for modern audiences (and even audiences when it was made). So she furfilled her ambition to study and speak like a lady so she can get a better job, why is she suddenly crying like marrying her teacher is the only option. She literally can get a much better job/life now. That setup sort of works in XIXth century setting - she worked her way to upper class and got a taste of it, but of course even if she can pass she doesn’t belong there because she doesn’t have money. But still you’d think the middle class world and a suitor of her choice would now be options, she can go work as a companion to some lady, get married eventually etc. But at emotional level that scene does make a lot of sense - “I’ve done this tough touch challenge and came out on the other side and now what? What do I do? Who am I?” But solving with bringing professor Higgins’ slippers makes no sense at all.

I watched it recently. I don't have much to say about it, except that I didn't like it. I love Audrey Hepburn, but the characters of this film were insufferable and the story drags for too long. And honestly it doesn't send a good message, but that's just me (this actually doesn't influence my opinion, but it's still a flaw for me). I know it's older, but it really looked like a more boring and overlong Pretty Woman to me.
I don't have issues with old films, musical, rom com and so on, it's just that I don't like this particular film.
